messages.author: 4f106c8e6f09dbec
messages.subject: No parallelisation in time-stratified analyses?
parts:
Hi all,

I have noticed that speed-up of analyses using parallelization doesn't seem to work for time-stratified analyses. Can anybody confirm that?

I am currently running the different possible perturbations of +d, +w, and time stratification on a big linux cluster. All non-stratified analyses make full use of the cores allocated (up to 64), whereas in the time-stratified analyses at least 90% of the cores are constantly idle.

Maybe time-stratification somehow prevents parallelization, or it hasn't been implemented yet for parallelization?

Cheers,
Ben

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: No parallelisation in time-stratified analyses?
parts:
I think the issue here is that only the "subtrees" get parallelized in a time-stratified analysis. 

Imagine taking a phylogeny, "chainsawing" it at various timepoints (10 mya, 20 mya etc.), and then looking at the collection of pieces.  Some of the pieces of the phylogeny would be single segments, some would be mini-phylogenies. 

Doing it this way, and keeping track of all of the pieces and all of the likelihoods flowing up and down all of the pieces (which is a huge pain) is basically a crazy way to do it, but it made some sense way back when I programmed it, given the weird APE phylo object structure.  But yeah, depending on the structure of the tree I think it will limit the value of parallelization as currently programmed.

Cheers,
Nick

messages.author: 95e9261d3e867527
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Re: No parallelisation in time-stratified analyses?
parts:
I have some related questions, as I getting ready to try time-stratified analysis on my dataset.

My tree is pretty large by typical BGB standards, I think (ca. 4,000 tips), with 9 areas. It took about a week running 30 cores to get DEC to finish without time-stratification.

My question is, will time-stratified analysis even be possible on this? I didn't realize until I saw Ben's post that the parallelization becomes slower (I suppose there's no way to know without trying though...)

A related question - I just tried setting up the analysis, and got this error:

"STOP ERROR in chainsaw2(): the post-chainsaw tree had 2 negative branchlengths. READ THE FOLLOWING ERROR MESSAGE SLOWLY AND CAREFULLY AND YOU
 MAY FIND A SOLUTION. This error seems to sometimes occur with large cuts on trees with many fossil tips (i.e., non-contemporaneous tips). I'
m not sure what causes the bug, except that chainsaw-ing an APE phylo object is quite complex, and it is even more complex for a tree with ma
ny non-contemporaneous tips. Imagine a phylogeny made of cardboard, then cutting it at various timepoints, then keeping track of all of the p
ieces.  Anyway, until I fix it, your best bet is to chainsaw2() in stages, using smaller cuts than the one that caused the error.  Or if you
are using BioGeoBEARS and doing a time-stratified analysis, create extra time-strata (perhaps repeating the same settings for several time bi
ns), so that the usage of chainsaw2() within section_the_tree() does not cause an error."                      

I currently have 7 time slices. I'm wondering if setting the number of slices lower (say 4) would help both possibly speed up the analysis and help with this error?

Anyways I will try these things, I was just thinking that Nick (or others) might have some insight that will help the analysis to finish.

Thanks!

- Joel

messages.author: 95e9261d3e867527
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Re: No parallelisation in time-stratified analyses?
parts:
Update: I was able to at least solve the "chainsaw2" error. I am sharing this in case it might help others who encounter this error.

It seems it was because although my tree was a dated tree that was ultrametric within rounding error, it was not exactly ultrametric. At least, ape::is.ultrametric() returned FALSE.

I made it truly ultrametric (so that ape::is.ultrametric() would return TRUE) with a custom function: https://gist.github.com/joelnitta/2db3a83538e79ee58ce71bdb1e551f2e

After that I was able to setup the BGB run without the "chainsaw2" error.

Next step is to see if I can get it to finish in a reasonable amount of time...
